pass_a_gloss: For lovers of lies and lusts—where drunkenness means fleshly death and excess means deadening the mind—You have awarded fitting punishment, in which Edom will take its place. The claim that it will not add to your banishment or return means this: since you do not persist in captivity, having met the full requirement, God lessens the penalty, He does not increase it. Thus, if this referred to a second exile that would never occur, how did the later one by Rome happen? Likely the discourse points to the ultimate event wrought through Christ, after which none followed. And "All Israel
pass_b_english: To those who love falsehoods and passions, of whom drunkenness is indeed the mortification of the flesh, and overflow is also the making dead of its mind—You have measured out sufficient justice, in which Edom shall receive its turn. And the statement that it will not add to your exile or to your restoration says this (for you do not remain in captivity, having fulfilled the full measure; for God diminishes the justice, He does not add to it), that is, if it was said toward a second captivity as one that would not come to pass, how then did the captivity after it come about through the Romans?
